newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Brit Biotech cost rise undramatic.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Brit Biotech cost rise undramatic.

text.p: Drug discovery company British Biotech Plc said on Wednesday it did not expect a dramatic rise in expenditure in the current year, despite preparing for the launch of its two lead drugs.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief executive Keith McCullagh said "there will be an increase in expenditure, but not dramatic."

In the year to April 30, British Biotech spent 48 million stg, with late-stage clinical trials and the establishment of an international marketing structure for pancreatitis drug Zacutex and cancer treatment Marimastat driving up costs.

However, the spending was partly offset by 8.4 million stg of milestone payments from collaborations with Glaxo Wellcome Plc and Japan's Tanabe Seiyaku Co Ltd, plus 9.8 million stg of interest on its cash pile, boosted by a 143 million stg rights issue a year ago.
McCullagh said with 183 million stg in the bank, British Biotech had "a very strong balance sheet. We are one of the most well-financed companies in the sector."

Data on the combination treatment trials was likely to be published at the main European cancer conference in the autumn. The company also intended to start work on slower acting cancers such as breast and colo-rectal, he said.

Zacutex, which would be British Biotech's first product on the market if it is approved by regulators, is expected to go on sale in Europe in 1998 and in the U.S. around 2000. The drug has already been submitted for approval in the European Union.
McCullagh said U.S. trials of the drug had been expanded to include 1,500 patients, with mortality rates against placebo the main comparison.

British Biotech said the decision to increase the trial sample to 1,500 patients from 450 had been taken after a U.S. data monitoring committee "noted that the overall incidence of death and serious organ failure in this trial was lower than predicted from the European studies".
McCullagh said that with the lead products now entering key phases the company would not "shower the market with news".
""We believe we have two excellent drugs in Phase III, with one going through registration. We think the market can judge the size and potential of these drugs."
